clue.text: Words taking up a hundred and one lines, fifty on soprano

indicators.note: the outer pair takes in, or holds, the other letters here
in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes above it

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: in a down clue, 'up' says these letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
I is the Roman numeral for one
RY, short for railway, the lines a train runs on

explanation.surface: A text that fills a hundred and one lines of verse, with a soprano singing fifty of them.
explanation.walkthrough: C, I and RY read upwards give YRIC; L above S then takes that in.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyrics of a song are its words, the text set to the music.

clue.text: Damage new judge ruled out lawfully

indicators.note: the letters for new and judge are excluded from the damage word

parts.note: to damage is to injure

explanation.surface: A newly appointed judge decides that some harm was done within the law.
explanation.walkthrough: IURE is Latin, as in 'de iure' (more often 'de jure'), so the answer is a legal Latin word rather than an English one.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin 'iure' means by right or by law, the ablative of 'ius', law.

clue.text: See off sweet man (not the royal one presumably!)

indicators.note: the letter for See comes off the front of the sweet

parts.note: candy is a sweet
the letter C is pronounced 'see'

explanation.surface: Dismissing a sugary man, presumably not a prince.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal Andy would be Prince Andrew, hence the joking aside; here it is just a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy is a common short form of Andrew, a man's first name.

clue.text: American school put up Trump campaign slogan

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales

explanation.surface: A US school displays a Trump election slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: A gam is a pod or school of whales, an old whaling word.
explanation.definitionFit: MAGA, short for 'Make America Great Again', was Donald Trump's campaign catchphrase.

clue.text: Boos in court — uneasy judge ultimately slammed challenge to authority

indicators.note: slammed means violently knocked about, so these letters are thrown into a new order
ultimately points to the final letter of judge

explanation.surface: A tennis crowd booing as an edgy umpire is shouted down.
explanation.walkthrough: John McEnroe's famous protest at a Wimbledon umpire's call, so the court, boos and judge all fit the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a famous disbelieving protest at an official's ruling, a defiance of authority.

clue.text: Try a somersault round lake — it's not pre-planned

indicators.note: the reversed letters are placed round the lake letter
a somersault turns things head over heels, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: to bid is to try, attempt

explanation.surface: An invitation to try a somersault near a lake, done on impulse.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ad-libbed is improvised on the spot, made up without preparation.

clue.text: Bet a rat chewed upholstery fabric

indicators.note: something chewed is mangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wager that a rodent has gnawed the sofa covering.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabaret is a striped silk fabric traditionally used for covering furniture.

clue.text: Points made by essentially twisted writer

indicators.note: only the inner part is given a twist, so the writer's letters are rearranged

parts.note: Martin or Kingsley Amis, the English novelists

explanation.surface: Arguments put forward by an author who is basically warped.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the middle pair of the novelist's name swaps over, which 'essentially' hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Aims are targets, the points something is directed at.

clue.text: Copper stops lodger in cycling event

indicators.note: the copper stops up, or plugs, the middle of the lodger word

parts.note: a Freemason belongs to a Lodge, so is jokingly a lodger
DI, Detective Inspector, a police officer

explanation.surface: A policeman halts a boarder during a bike race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like Cu, the metal; it is a police detective.
explanation.definitionFit: The madison is a track cycling relay race named after Madison Square Garden.

clue.text: So directly related to work colleague

parts.note: one's line is one's line of work
an ally is an associate or colleague

explanation.surface: Thus closely linked to a fellow worker.
explanation.definitionFit: Lineally means by direct descent, in an unbroken line of ancestry, and 'so' makes the definition an adverb.

clue.text: Make love to actor

parts.note: a make is a brand, a manufacturer's name
love is zero in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: An invitation to romance a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlon Brando was the American film star of The Godfather.

clue.text: Removing clothes, seduced maybe 20, we hear

definitions.note: 20 across is MANN, which sounds like Man, and the Isle of Man is one such island

indicators.note: the outer letters are its clothing, so they are stripped off

parts.note: seduced means misled, led astray

explanation.surface: Undressing, someone led astray, perhaps by a German author, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference is to 20 across, the writer Thomas Mann; said aloud his name is Man, the island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: An isle is an island, and the Isle of Man is an example.

clue.text: Frame slippery character when arrested

indicators.note: the eel has the word for when held inside it, like a prisoner

parts.note: an eel is a notoriously slippery creature
as can mean when, as in 'as he left'

explanation.surface: Setting up a crook who was caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frame' looks like a verb about fitting someone up; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a stand or frame that holds a painter's canvas.

clue.text: See 5
Barge pump possibly captivates Victor

indicators.note: to captivate is to capture, so the shoe holds Victor inside

parts.note: a pump is a type of shoe
V is Victor in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A canal boat whose pump has a man called Victor spellbound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barge' and 'pump' suggest a boat and its machinery; barge is the verb, to push.
explanation.definitionFit: To barge is to push roughly, to shove one's way through.

clue.text: Old fellow avoided seafood

indicators.note: the fellow letter is avoided, so it is left out

parts.note: former means old, previous

explanation.surface: An elderly man steered clear of the shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: An ormer is an abalone, an edible sea snail prized in the Channel Islands.

clue.text: Weak leader ignoring commotion — wimp!

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for weak, as in the physicists' weak force

indicators.note: the leader of the commotion word is its first letter, the one to go
the commotion word ignores, drops, the letter named by leader

parts.note: a fuss is a commotion

explanation.surface: A feeble chief who shrugs off a disturbance is a coward.
explanation.definitionFit: A wuss is a slang term for a feeble, timid person.

clue.text: Scold after violent pub attack

indicators.note: violent means the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: a raid is an attack

explanation.surface: Telling someone off following a brutal assault on a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: To upbraid someone is to reprimand them sharply.

clue.text: Invited to be suspicious about story — and confirmation it's worked?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, or around, the story
suspicious suggests something fishy, a sign to rearrange the letters

parts.note: a story is a lie, a fib

explanation.surface: Asked to be doubtful of a tale, and then told it succeeded.
explanation.walkthrough: Victor Meldrew's catchphrase in the sitcom One Foot in the Grave; the question mark admits the exclamation of disbelief can greet success.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation of astonishment is what someone might gasp on seeing an unlikely plan succeed.

clue.text: Smart boy turned up in India and another country

indicators.note: the reversed name goes inside the India letters
in a down clue, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a smart Alec is a know-all, so Alec is the smart boy

explanation.surface: A clever lad shows up in India and somewhere else too.
explanation.definitionFit: Iceland is a Nordic island nation, a country other than India.

clue.text: Writer's piece finally repeated

parts.note: a man is a piece in chess or draughts
the final letter of the chess piece written once more, so the last letter appears twice

explanation.surface: An author's work ends with a repetition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' looks like the writer's work; it is a chess piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Mann was the German novelist who wrote Death in Venice and The Magic Mountain.

clue.text: See 19
Government not about to capture hearts — it has minimal backing

indicators.note: the reversed letters capture, or hold, the hearts letter
about means the letters are turned round

parts.note: H is the card-game abbreviation for hearts

explanation.surface: A government declining to win over the public's affections.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a joke: a thong is a garment with very little fabric at the back.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong is skimpy underwear or swimwear that leaves the rear almost bare.

clue.text: Minister at sea shows that's annoying

indicators.note: the answer shows itself within the words Minister at sea

explanation.surface: A government minister out of their depth reveals irritation.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Rats!' is a mild exclamation of annoyance or disappointment.

clue.text: Bind over male — offensive, right?

indicators.note: in a down clue the offensive comes over, above, the male

parts.note: the Tet Offensive of the Vietnam War
he is a male

explanation.surface: A legal binding-over of a man for being offensive, rightly so?
explanation.walkthrough: 'offensive' looks like an adjective; it is the noun, the 1968 Tet Offensive.
explanation.definitionFit: To tether is to tie up or restrain, as with an animal on a rope.

clue.text: Loathing one on benefit in North America

indicators.note: the inner pieces sit inside North America
one placed on, beside, the benefit

parts.note: a means one
use is benefit, as in 'of no use'

explanation.surface: Someone on welfare in the US and Canada feels disgust.
explanation.definitionFit: Nausea is sickness, and figuratively strong disgust or revulsion.

clue.text: John supporting southern European

indicators.note: in a down clue the john sits below the southern letter, supporting it

parts.note: a john is a lavatory, lav for short

explanation.surface: A man called John backs someone from southern Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like a man's name; it is the US slang word for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A Slav belongs to a group of peoples of central and eastern Europe.

clue.text: Cupids in Rome at it surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at letters in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: Little love gods unexpectedly at work in Rome.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoretti are cherubs, small winged figures of the god of love in Italian art.

clue.text: Board game not hard? It was a battle

indicators.note: not hard means the hard letter is left out

parts.note: halma is a board game, a forerunner of Chinese chequers
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A board game that is easy, though it felt like a struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alma was an 1854 Crimean War battle, fought on the river of that name.

clue.text: Island to north that is going to be unoccupied

indicators.note: in a down clue, going to the north means reading upwards
an unoccupied word has its insides removed, leaving only its outer letters

explanation.surface: An island to the north that will soon be left empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Eigg is one of the Small Isles of the Inner Hebrides off Scotland's west coast.

clue.text: Thought mount should get over fence at the rear

indicators.note: the mountain straddles, gets over, the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: Mount Ida, in Crete and in Turkey

indicators.note: the rear of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A horse should be able to clear the last fence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mount' looks like a horse jumping a fence; it is Mount Ida.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought, a notion formed in the mind.

clue.text: Agitator during protest has silver tongue? Not half!

indicators.note: silver comes during, inside, the protest

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: not half of the word, so only its back half is used

explanation.surface: A rabble-rouser at a demonstration is a smooth talker, and how!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' is British slang for 'very much so', but here it drops the front half of tongue to leave GUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A demagogue is a political agitator who stirs up crowds with emotional appeals.
